title: Past Perfect
tagline: the earlier past: had + past participle
why: When you tell a story, the past perfect shows which thing happened first. It helps the listener follow the order of events without confusion.
know: the form: had + past participle (had left, had seen, had finished)
the signal words by the time, already, before, after, never ... before
understand: the difference between When I arrived, she left (she left after I came) and When I arrived, she had left (she left before I came)
why we often don't need the past perfect when before or after already makes the order clear
able: tell a story with two past times and make the order clear
explain a past situation: I was hungry because I hadn't eaten.
talk about first experiences: I had never seen snow before I came to Canada.
mistakes: When I arrived, she already left.
When I arrived, she had already left.
By the time we got to the station, the train left.
By the time we got to the station, the train had left.
I was nervous because I never flew before.
I was nervous because I had never flown before.
Did you had finished when he called?
use: the earlier of two past actions: When we got to the cinema, the film had already started.
with by the time: By the time the ambulance came, he had stopped breathing.
to explain a reason in the past: She was upset because she had lost her ring.
experience up to a past moment: I had never eaten sushi before that night.
form: I / you / he / she / we / they had finished. Short form: I'd finished.
tip: Draw a time line. The past simple is your main story point; the past perfect goes one step further back. When I got home, my wife cooked dinner (after I came). When I got home, my wife had cooked dinner (it was ready).

pick.q: When we got to the party, most of the guests ___ home.
pick.why: The guests went home before we arrived, so we use the earlier past: had gone.

pick.q: By the time I found my glasses, the show ___.
pick.why: By the time + past simple usually needs the past perfect for the earlier action: had ended.

pick.q: I didn't recognize him because he ___ a beard.
pick.why: He grew the beard before I saw him. The earlier past is had grown.

pick.q: She ___ never driven in snow before that winter.
pick.why: Experience up to a past moment ('before that winter') uses had + past participle.

pick.q: They were hungry because they ___ breakfast.
pick.why: The reason happened earlier than 'were hungry', so we use the past perfect: hadn't had.

pick.q: ___ you ever been to Europe before that trip?
pick.why: 'Before that trip' points to a time before a past moment, so we ask with Had + past participle.

pick.q: I called the store, but it ___ already closed.
pick.why: The store closed before I called, so we use had + past participle: had already closed.

pick.q: After he ___ the report, he sent it to his manager.
pick.why: Had + past participle. Write, wrote, written, so: had written.

type.q: When I checked my phone, I saw that my sister ___ (call) three times.
type.why: The calls came before I checked, so we use the past perfect: had called.

type.q: When we got to the restaurant, we realized we ___ (not / book) a table.
type.why: Not booking happened before we got there. Negative past perfect: hadn't booked.

type.q: By the time the firefighters arrived, the fire ___ (spread) to the garage.
type.why: By the time + past simple: the earlier action uses had + past participle: had spread.

type.q: I was nervous because I ___ (never / speak) in public before.
type.why: Experience before a past moment: had never + past participle. Speak, spoke, spoken.

type.q: ___ (you / finish) your homework when your friends came over?
type.why: Past perfect question: Had + subject + past participle.

type.q: He reached for his wallet and realized he ___ (leave) it at home.
type.why: Leaving the wallet at home happened before he realized it: had left.

type.q: The house was quiet. Everyone ___ (go) to bed.
type.why: They went to bed before this moment. Go, went, gone: had gone.

type.q: She didn't understand the joke because she ___ (not / see) the film before.
type.why: Negative past perfect: hadn't + past participle. See, saw, seen.

spot.q: When I got to the office, the meeting already started.
spot.why: The meeting started before I arrived, so we need the past perfect: had already started.

spot.q: I had forgot my password, so I couldn't log in.
spot.why: After had we use the past participle. Forget, forgot, forgotten: had forgotten.

spot.q: By the time we reached the beach, the sun went down.
spot.why: With by the time, the earlier action uses the past perfect: had gone down.

spot.q: Did you had eaten before you came?
spot.why: Past perfect questions start with Had, not Did: Had you eaten?

spot.q: He was tired because he didn't sleep for two days.
spot.why: Two days up to a past moment uses the past perfect: hadn't slept.

order.a: Had you met her before the wedding?
order.why: Past perfect question: Had + subject + past participle + time.

order.a: The bus had already left when we arrived.
alt: When we arrived the bus had already left.
order.why: Earlier action (had already left) + when + later action (arrived).

order.a: I had never seen the ocean before.
order.why: Subject + had never + past participle + before.

order.a: She hadn't told anyone about the baby.
order.why: Negative past perfect: subject + hadn't + past participle.

pick.q: When I opened the fridge, I saw that someone ___ my yogurt.
pick.why: Someone ate it before I opened the fridge: had eaten.

pick.q: By the time the police came, the thief ___.
pick.why: By the time + past simple: the earlier action uses the past perfect: had escaped.

pick.q: We ___ never tried poutine before we moved to Quebec.
pick.why: Experience before a past moment uses had + past participle: had never tried.

pick.q: I was late because I ___ the wrong bus.
pick.why: Had + past participle. Take, took, taken: had taken.

pick.q: The kitchen was a mess. The kids ___ cookies.
pick.why: They made the cookies before this past moment, so we use had made.

pick.q: ___ she left by the time you got there?
pick.why: By the time + past simple: the question uses Had + past participle.

type.q: When we got to the gate, the plane ___ (already / take off).
type.why: The plane took off before we arrived: had already taken off.

type.q: I ___ (not / understand) the instructions, so I asked again.
type.why: Both work: hadn't understood (earlier past) or didn't understand. The past perfect shows the order.

type.q: That evening she realized that her boyfriend ___ (forget) her birthday.
type.why: Forgetting happened before she realized it. Forget, forgot, forgotten: had forgotten.

type.q: By the time I woke up, my husband ___ (make) breakfast.
type.why: By the time + past simple: the earlier action uses had + past participle: had made.

type.q: ___ (they / leave) by the time you got to the office?
type.why: By the time + past simple: the question uses Had + subject + past participle. Leave, left, left.

type.q: It was my first time in a canoe. I ___ (never / paddle) before.
type.why: Experience up to a past moment: had never + past participle.

type.q: When I looked outside, I saw that it ___ (rain) in the night.
type.why: The rain came before I looked outside: had rained.

type.q: We ___ (not / finish) the project when the deadline came.
type.why: Negative past perfect up to a past moment: hadn't finished.

spot.q: When my parents arrived, I already cleaned the house.
spot.why: I cleaned before my parents arrived, so we need the past perfect: had already cleaned.

spot.q: She had wrote three emails before lunch.
spot.why: After had we use the past participle. Write, wrote, written: had written.

spot.q: I didn't know the way because I never was there before.
spot.why: Experience before a past moment: had never been.

spot.q: By the time the guests arrived, we have finished cooking.
spot.why: In a past story, by the time needs had, not have: we had finished.

order.a: Had they eaten before the movie started?
order.why: Past perfect question: Had + subject + past participle + before + past simple.

order.a: I realized that I had lost my phone.
order.why: Past simple (realized) + that + past perfect (had lost) for the earlier action.

order.a: We hadn't seen each other for years.
alt: For years we hadn't seen each other.
order.why: Negative past perfect: subject + hadn't + past participle + time.

bank.q: When we reached the store, it ___ out of milk.
bank.why: Had + past participle. Run, ran, run: had run.

bank.q: By the time the doctor saw me, I ___ for three hours.
bank.why: By the time + past simple: the earlier time uses the past perfect: had waited.

bank.q: He ___ never played hockey before he came to Canada.
bank.why: Experience before a past moment uses had + past participle: had never played.

bank.q: I couldn't get in because I ___ my key.
bank.why: Losing the key happened before I tried to get in: had lost.

bank.q: ___ you heard the news before I told you?
bank.why: 'Before I told you' is a past moment, so the question uses Had + past participle.

bank.q: When I saw the bill, I knew I ___ too much.
bank.why: The spending came before I saw the bill: had spent.

bank.q: The roads were icy because it ___ below zero all night.
bank.why: The cold night came before the icy roads in the past: had been.

bank.q: She was sad because her cat ___.
bank.why: The cat died before she was sad, so we use the earlier past: had died.

bank.q: When I got to the bank, it ___ (close).
bank.why: The bank closed before I arrived: had closed.

bank.q: I felt terrible at work because I ___ (not / sleep) for two nights.
bank.why: Two nights up to a past moment uses the past perfect: hadn't slept.

bank.q: By the time we found a seat, the speaker ___ (begin).
bank.why: Begin, began, begun. By the time + past simple needs had begun.

bank.q: ___ (he / ever / ride) a horse before that day?
bank.why: Past perfect question: Had + subject + ever + past participle. Ride, rode, ridden.

bank.q: When I got home, I saw that my wife ___ (plant) new flowers.
bank.why: She planted them before I got home: had planted.

bank.q: When the taxi came, we already said goodbye.
bank.why: We said goodbye before the taxi came: had already said.

bank.q: I had took the medicine before I went to bed.
bank.why: After had we use the past participle: had taken.

bank.q: By the time I got home, the kids had gone to sleep.
bank.why: This sentence is correct: by the time + past simple, with the earlier action in the past perfect (had gone).

bank.q: She told me she had never seen a moose before.
bank.why: This sentence is correct: had never seen shows experience before the past moment of telling.

bank.a: Had you already eaten when they arrived?
bank.why: Past perfect question: Had + subject + already + past participle + when + past simple.

bank.a: They had sold the house before we called.
alt: Before we called they had sold the house.
bank.why: Earlier action (had sold) + before + later action (called).

bank.a: I hadn't heard that song in years.
bank.why: Negative past perfect: subject + hadn't + past participle + time.
